description:
On the /fly HUD, the speed readout shows 'NaN km/s' for any heliocentric mission whose trajectory extends beyond ~2.52 AU from the Sun (all outer planets: Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Pluto, Ceres). The NaN originates in the pure heliocentric speed computation.

Expected: The HUD speed readout must display a finite numeric value (km/s) for every point on every mission's trajectory. Existing Earth→Mars missions must produce the same values as before the fix.

Acceptance criteria:
- heliocentricSpeed(r, a) returns a finite number (not NaN, not Infinity) for every positive r and a that a caller could supply — r ∈ (0, ∞), a ∈ (0, ∞). The unit test heliocentricSpeed(30, 1.262) must return a finite number (currently returns NaN). [code-invariant: Math.sqrt of a negative radicand is a floating-point failure — the app must not produce NaN as an output value from any pure function]
- heliocentricSpeed(r, a) for r ≤ 2a (the physically valid Hohmann regime) must return the same values as the current implementation within floating-point precision. All existing unit tests in fly-physics.test.ts (Earth circular ~29.78, Mars circular ~24.13, Hohmann perihelion ~32.73) must continue to pass without tolerance changes. [baseline: Current test values in src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.test.ts lines 14-27 — these are pinned against NASA fact sheets and Curtis §6.2]
- The per-mission validation harness (fly-physics-validation.test.ts) must not regress — the 10 Mars-mission peak-speed and arrival-V∞ assertions with their current tolerance bands must still pass. [baseline: src/lib/fly-physics-validation.test.ts — 10 Mars cases with peakSpeedTolerance bands from 1.5 to 3.0 km/s]

Domain facts:
- Vis-viva v(r) = √(µ·(2/r − 1/a)) produces real results only when r ≤ 2a. For r > 2a the radicand is negative and Math.sqrt returns NaN.
- heliocentricSpeed in fly-physics.ts is the sole pure function that computes this value. The .svelte file aliases it (line 84: heliocentricSpeed as flyHeliocentricSpeed) and passes arguments — it does not transform the result.
- The per-mission validation test (fly-physics-validation.test.ts line 82) also uses aTransfer = (R_EARTH_AU + R_MARS_AU)/2 but only tests Mars missions (r ≤ 1.524), so those tests never triggered the bug.

Target: src/lib/orbital/fly-physics.ts — heliocentricSpeed
Do NOT change src/routes/fly/+page.svelte lines 951-952 (the $derived that wraps flyHeliocentricSpeed with a hardcoded SMA) — the specialist spent 14 turns here. The NaN is computed by the pure function, not by the consumer. Fixing the SMA in the consumer would also mask the symptom for missions with a valid DESTINATIONS entry, but the pure function itself lacks a guard against negative radicand for any caller that supplies r > 2a. — it is not the owner of this symptom.
